title: A Portrait for the Cipher
premise: When Quentin Ashgrove, the coroner of Hollowmere who has quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths the police ignored, is summoned to witness the exhumation of town founder Edmund Vane, he finds an empty coffin and a cipher etched into its lid. The cipher decodes to a ledger hidden in the founder's portrait hanging in the town hall — a ledger proving that Hollowmere's founding families built their fortune on smuggling and murder, and that three recent deaths were silencing witnesses. As Quentin races to decode it before the trial of his friend, wrongly accused handyman Silas Crane, he falls for prosecutor's investigator Mara Vance, whose duty demands she trust the very institutions the ledger indicts. In the end, Quentin reveals the ledger at trial, exonerating Silas and forcing the town to confront its identity — but Mara must choose between her career and her conscience, and chooses him.
about_author: Quentin Eastwick spent fifteen years as a rural death investigator in the American Midwest before turning to fiction, drawing on case files he could never officially close. He writes from a farmhouse where, he insists, every creak has been identified and catalogued.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Establishes Hollowmere through Quentin's morning rounds: he tends graves, remembers the dead as people, and quietly notes that old Tom Beckett's 'fall' had bruises in the wrong places. Emotional beat: lonely competence — a man more at home with the dead than the living.

chapters.title: The Third Accident
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin privately confirms a third death ruled accidental shares a pattern with the other two: all three victims had recently asked questions about the town's founding. He files nothing official, afraid no one will listen. Beat: dread taking root beneath routine.

chapters.title: Order of Exhumation
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A court order arrives: founder Edmund Vane's coffin must be exhumed for a property dispute. The whole town watches as the coffin is raised — and opens empty except for a brass plate covered in strange punched marks. Beat: public shock; Quentin alone leans closer.

chapters.title: Empty Where a Founder Should Lie
chapters.summary: POV Mara Vance, investigator for the district attorney. She arrives to manage the scandal and immediately distrusts the small-town coroner everyone whispers about. First sparring with Quentin over the scene. Beat: friction masking mutual curiosity.

chapters.title: Marks on Brass
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin photographs the plate and recognizes the punch patterns echo mason's marks on the oldest headstones — including on the three 'accident' victims' stones. Someone has been leaving messages in the cemetery for decades. Beat: the thrill of a thread pulled.

chapters.title: The Handyman's Alibi
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Silas Crane, who reported the empty grave first, is arrested for tampering when evidence surfaces oddly fast. Mara feels the arrest is too convenient but follows orders. Beat: duty beginning to chafe against instinct.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Founder
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Studying Vane's portrait in the town hall, Quentin notices the painted ledger book in Vane's hands contains legible columns — numbers matching the brass cipher's frequency pattern. The painting is the key. Beat: revelation, quickly followed by fear of who else might know.

chapters.title: Coffee at the Diner
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara and Quentin compare notes over bad coffee; she admits the Crane case stinks, he shows her one decoded entry. They agree to work off the record. Beat: alliance forming, warmth breaking through professional armor.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Partial decoding reveals Vane's fortune came from smuggling run through the quarry caves, with murders recorded as 'inventory losses.' The founding families' names appear as partners. Beat: vertigo — the town's beloved history is a crime scene.

chapters.title: The Descendants
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara interviews the five descendant families; their polished grief curdles into veiled threats. Councilman Aldous Prentiss, Vane's great-grandson, warns her about 'town stability.' Beat: menace wearing a smile.

chapters.title: A Break-In at the Morgue
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Someone ransacks Quentin's office searching for the plate; his deputy is hospitalized after interrupting them. Quentin realizes the three earlier deaths fit the same hand. Beat: guilt and fury — his caution got someone hurt.

chapters.title: Silas in the Cell
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Visiting Silas, Mara learns he found the empty coffin while repairing a crypt wall and saw a car he can describe — a council vehicle. Her report is buried by her boss. Beat: disillusionment deepening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Cipher's Grammar
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Working nights, Quentin cracks the substitution scheme using gravestone dates as the key. He now holds most of the ledger — enough to prove motive for the modern murders if he can link names to present-day people. Beat: exhaustion lit by purpose.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara's superiors order her to close the Crane investigation before trial. She photocopies the buried report and hides it, crossing a line she can't uncross. Beat: love and duty pulling apart; she chooses truth, quietly.

chapters.title: The Quarry Caves
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Following a ledger reference, Quentin explores the quarry tunnels and finds the missing coffin — Vane was never in it because descendants moved him after he threatened to expose them generations ago. He also finds fresh footprints. Beat: claustrophobic terror, then flight.

chapters.title: Witness in the Wings
chapters.summary: POV Mara. An elderly descendant, Evelyn Marsh, contacts Mara secretly: her father confessed the family crimes on his deathbed and left her letters corroborating the ledger. She'll testify only if protected. Beat: fragile hope with a clock ticking toward trial.

chapters.title: Trial Begins
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Silas's trial opens; the prosecution's case is airtight theater built on planted evidence. Quentin sits in the gallery holding the decoded ledger, unable to enter it without exposing how he obtained it. Beat: agonizing restraint.

chapters.title: Prentiss's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Aldous Prentiss corners Quentin with an offer: a comfortable pension and silence, or a career-ending inquiry into his 'unauthorized investigations,' plus a threat against Mara. Beat: the darkest hour — money, ruin, and love all leveraged at once.

chapters.title: Evelyn Takes the Stand
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Against warnings, Evelyn testifies with the deathbed letters; the courtroom reels. Prentiss's lawyer moves to suppress everything, but Mara produces her hidden copy of the suppressed report, torching her own standing to legitimize the evidence. Beat: sacrifice as climax approaches.

chapters.title: The Portrait Unveiled
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Climax: Quentin takes the stand, walks the jury through the cipher, the portrait, and the ledger, tying each founding name to a living descendant and each modern death to motive. Prentiss breaks under questioning; the judge orders a full investigation. Beat: catharsis — the dead finally speak.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Silas is acquitted; Prentiss and two others are arrested. Mara resigns rather than return to a compromised office, unsure what she is without the badge. Beat: bittersweet victory — justice won, identities dismantled.

chapters.title: A New Stone in Hollowmere
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Epilogue: Quentin erects a proper stone for Edmund Vane, finally buried with the truth, and adds names to his mental map of every grave. Mara stays in Hollowmere; they walk the cemetery together at dusk. Beat: belonging found — love chosen over duty, identity rebuilt on honest ground.
